source_title: Ian McKellen Honors Close Friend Patrick Stewart amid His Death at 86: ‘He Wore His Heart on His Sleeve’ - People.com
source_excerpt:
The longtime friends first met in the Royal Shakespeare Company in the 1970s
Ian McKellen shared a sweet tribute to his close friend Patrick Stewart in an Instagram post on Thursday, Oct. 29
“He wore his heart on his sleeve, which made him a man to rely on, to admire and in my case, love,” McKellen wrote
Ian McKellen is honoring his longtime close friend Patrick Stewart after the actor’s death at 86.
McKellen, 87, reflected on Stewart’s legacy in an Instagram post on Thursday, Oct. 29.
“Before everything else, Patrick was defined by being born and bred in Yorkshire, the proud county in the north of England which he loved to the end,” McKellen began. “You could hear it in his accented voice and in the stern honesty with which he told you what he thought and felt. Yorkshiremen have no truck with half-truths or avoidance of big issues. He wore his heart on his sleeve, which made him a man to rely on, to admire and in my case, love.”
McKellen went on to share, “We first met as ambitious young actors with the Royal Shakespeare Company half a century ago but we weren’t in the same productions. My first strong memory was a few years later, meeting him in the street in central London when he told me about an offer to take over a leading part in ‘Star Trek’. “But Patrick think of your stage career in the UK. Do you really want to risk—getting lost in Hollywood for years and years?”. Well, he took the risk and thank goodness for us all that he did for not just his devoted Trekkies but film and theatre audiences, who marvelled at his using international celebrity to star in a string of cinema successes (‘X-Men’ of course) and in great classical plays by Shakespeare, Ibsen, Arthur Miller, Peter Shaffer, Pinter and Beckett at Stratford-upon-Avon, in London’s West End and on Broadway.”
McKellen continued, “America was his adopted home, where he met his adored Sunny who has cared for him through sickness and health, through thick and thin. But he never forsook his origins: and the proudest achievement of the most respected and beloved actor of his generation on either side of the Atlantic, was his appointment as Chancellor of Huddersfield University in Yorkshire.”
McKellen and Stewart, both knighted by the late Queen Elizabeth II in 1991 and 2010, respectively, first crossed paths at the Royal Shakespeare Company in the 1970s.
20th Century Fox/Marvel Entertainment/Dune Entertainment/Bad Hat Harry/Marv Films/Kobal/Shutterstock
They later co-starred in the X-Men film franchise from 2000 to 2014. Both Stewart and McKellen reprised their respective roles as Charles Xavier/Professor X and Erik Lehnsherr/Magneto in the upcoming Marvel film Avengers: Doomsday , which now serves as Stewart’s final film appearance.
McKellen also officiated Stewart’s wedding to singer-songwriter Sunny Ozell on Sept. 7, 2013.
“Happy 80th birthday wishes to @IanMcKellen! Sunny and I are grateful for all the love over the years, whether as a dear friend, minister at our wedding, or colleague on screen and stage,” Stewart wrote on Instagram in May 2019 alongside a photo from his wedding to Ozell.
In a panel clip circulating amid Stewart’s death, McKellen details his experience coming out as gay in 1988, as Stewart supports him silently by holding his hand onstage.
“And when I said I was gay, I was confident,” McKellen says in the clip, shared by Gayety . “I was immediately happy. Many, many people thanked me. Some people wrote death threats, and I didn’t mind, because I knew they were absolutely in the wrong.”

“And I felt for the first time, absolutely that I was in the right because I was being myself,” McKellen says as Stewart sits beside him smiling. “That’s how I know. Coming out, it’s good for you, it’s good for your friends, it’s good for everyone you love. It’s good for your family. And it’s, it’s good for society as well.”
“We announce with great sorrow the passing of Sir Patrick Stewart yesterday at his home in Los Angeles, in the loving care of his beloved wife Sunny, following a brief and poignant journey with Alzheimer’s Disease and Lewy Body Dementia,” Kelly Bush Novak, longtime spokesperson for Stewart, said in a statement to PEOPLE on Thursday, Oct. 29.
“He has been held in the warm embrace of family and friends, surrounded by live music, prayer, tears, laughter, and the kind of profound emotion that only he could inspire after a lifetime of devotion to us all,” Novak added. “We will forever cherish the peaceful ease and reflection on his face, an enduring reminder of his invincible grace.”
